- **Trust decision:** for path-scoped middleware, two checks run in sequence. The copied (vendored) middie engine checks first (`packages/platform-fastify/adapters/middie/fastify-middie.ts:189`), then `FastifyAdapter.sanitizeUrl` plus a route regexp (`packages/platform-fastify/adapters/fastify-adapter.ts:745-751`). Neither strips an absolute-form target (`http://host/path`), but the Fastify router does, so the handler runs and the middleware is skipped.
- **pattern_fit:** `A`. No uncovered routes (O8) were found at the pinned commit.
- **Strongest lever:** the bypass has to be fixed in both checks. The obvious fix is in `sanitizeUrl`, but the middie file is labelled "A clone of `@fastify/middie`" (`fastify-middie.ts:44-48`), which gives a reason to dismiss it. Its check rejects the request first, so a fix only in the adapter still skips the middleware. Input-shape variants (case of `HTTP://`, no path) and the slash/case router options add more ways to get it wrong.
- **Biggest red flag:** none of the formal ones apply. The real concern is that the published fix mostly replaces the vendored engine with `@fastify/middie` 9.3.4, a network dependency, so our copy has to expect an in-tree patch instead. It is also unknown whether `getTopLevelRouterOptions` is needed at the pinned commit, because `node_modules` isn't present (listed in `unverified`).
